title: A return to HELM’s original design
summary: The original helm emblem, warm neutral colors, and simpler homepage return, with the current guidance and shared skills easy to find.

items.text: The homepage brings back the compact HELM introduction, six principle cards, and direct practitioner and leadership paths. A short proposal example explains how delegation, review, and human responsibility fit together.

The helm emblem, cream background, and terracotta accents carry through the navigation, guides, browser icon, and shared-link previews. Current content, source notes, roles, and shared-skill practice guides remain available.

title: Clearer site navigation
summary: A more compact header highlights your current section, with larger navigation targets and a simpler mobile menu.

items.text: The header now highlights the section you are reading. On smaller screens, guides appear in a single list, and the menu closes with Escape or a tap outside it. Navigation remains available without JavaScript.

title: A new HELM wordmark
summary: HELM has a compact new wordmark, with matching browser and link-preview images to help you recognize the site and shared guides.

sections.heading: Recognize HELM when reading and sharing

items.text: The new lettering appears in the header and footer across the site. A matching H identifies browser tabs, and shared links use the same wordmark.

title: A clearer starting point for changing work
summary: The homepage now connects HELM’s principles to everyday questions about delegation, review, and responsibility across teams.

items.text: Follow an illustrative customer proposal from a shared brief through agent drafting, cross-team review, and a human decision. Each handoff explains what the person owns and what the agent does.

Find the six principles, practitioner and leadership paths, and roles and shared-skills resources in a new page layout. The role guides remain focused on engineering and product; shared-skills examples also include content, sales, and account management.
A consistent visual style connects the homepage and guides, with clearer headings and navigation. The proposal example also remains readable without JavaScript.

title: HELM’s start and first launch
summary: HELM started in October 2025 and first launched on 1 April 2026.

items.text: The Updates page now includes dated entries for HELM’s initial draft in October 2025 and first public launch on 1 April 2026, before the first numbered release on 5 September 2026.

title: Keeping HELM simple
summary: HELM 1.0.1 is easier to read and use, with simpler principles, practical guides, shared skills, and a focused roadmap.

items.text: Start with six principles written in everyday language, each with a small action to try. The guides explain how to use the advice with your team.

The role guides now focus on responsibilities, relevant experience and learning. The same five shared competencies appear across the site, and examples make clear what the guidance does and does not establish.
Further reading offers extra context and simple reminders for adapting the guidance without presenting every suggestion as a guaranteed result.
Choose a skill and your role to get practical steps, an example, an exercise for your next task, and a short self-check.

links.label: Find a guide for your skill and role

items.text: The roadmap focuses on clearer guidance, a shared-competency development review to try with people across roles, and a possible short playbook for one piece of work.
Follow one dated update with direct links to everything included in this release, or subscribe to future published updates.

title: A shared starting point for human–agent teamwork
summary: The first numbered release brings HELM’s principles, practical guides, and role descriptions together, so your team can refer to the same version when discussing how to work with AI agents.

sections.heading: A common language for your team

items.text: Explore six principles for decisions about AI-assisted work, from choosing simple approaches to keeping people accountable for results.
Use the Practitioner Guide to discuss how agents fit a workflow, how results should be checked, and where people need to make decisions.
Explore ownership, adoption, and measurement with the Leadership Guide, including questions to consider as your team changes how it works.
Explore how responsibilities and competencies may change across engineering, product, and design when agents become part of the work.
This release established a common reference for discussion and local testing. Teams still needed to try the guidance against their own work, and several recommendations were scheduled for review.

title: First public launch
summary: HELM first launched publicly on 1 April 2026. The first numbered release, HELM 1.0.0, followed in September 2026.

title: Initial draft
summary: Work on HELM began in October 2025, ahead of its first public launch in April 2026.
